why: Each value covers the interval from its first to its last occurrence; any values whose intervals overlap must end up as the same value. Merging overlapping intervals (the partition-labels sweep) gives the groups, and each group of g distinct values costs g - 1 replacements.
hints: If value v appears at positions i < j, what must every element between i and j become in the final array?

All of them must end up with v's final value. Replace each value by its [first, last] span; overlapping spans chain into one group that must collapse to a single value, while separate segments can stay distinct.

Record last occurrence of each value, sweep left to right extending the current segment's end to the max last occurrence seen, and close a segment when i reaches its end. Answer = distinct values - number of segments. O(n).
pitfalls: A value nested inside another's span still has to merge: in [1, 2, 2, 1], 1 appears in two blocks until 2 becomes 1 (or 1 becomes 2).
Overlap is transitive: [1, 2, 1, 3, 2, 3] is one group even though 1 and 3 never interleave directly.
One operation removes one distinct value, so a group of g values needs g - 1 operations, not the number of bad positions.
